clue.text: Check on one's story?

parts.note: a check is a block or obstruction, and one's story belongs to a writer: the obstruction an author meets when the words will not come

explanation.surface: Someone verifying the truth of a person's account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as verifying, but here it means a stoppage, and 'one's story' points to the person who writes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the creative paralysis in which an author cannot produce new work, a check on their story-telling.

clue.text: Football club initially forecast to draw, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters gathered here could be arranged another way
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word forecast

explanation.surface: A pools punter predicting that a certain football team will draw its match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges F (the first letter of 'forecast', picked by 'initially') with TODRAW into the club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Watford FC is an English professional football club from Hertfordshire, nicknamed the Hornets.

clue.text: I sounded German out to acquire land

indicators.note: out tells us the German letter is to be removed from what precedes it

parts.note: a bell that sounded rang

explanation.surface: Someone who rang the German side, trying to buy a piece of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes G (German) from I RANG, leaving the country; 'to acquire' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in the Middle East, and a country is a land.

clue.text: Hide notes containing excerpts

indicators.note: containing says the two notes hold the excerpts between them

parts.note: E is a musical note, and two of them give the plural
clips are short excerpts from a film or broadcast

explanation.surface: Concealing written memos that include extracts from documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts CLIPS between E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to obscure or block it from view, as the moon blots out the sun.

clue.text: Record collection losing money

parts.note: a set is a collection of things that belong together
if you are down, you are out of pocket

explanation.surface: A record collector selling discs at a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to write it as a record, as in setting down one's thoughts on paper.

clue.text: Sounds like he's one deceiving music producer

indicators.note: Sounds like tells us the word for a deceiver is spoken, then spelt differently

parts.note: a man who deceives is a liar

explanation.surface: A remark that a record producer is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' turns the deceiver into the stringed instrument, which is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient harp-like stringed instrument, an object that makes music.

clue.text: A quarter raised in rough campaign

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for rough

parts.note: crude means rough or unrefined

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A rough part of town stirred into a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A S into SA in this down clue, and 'in' puts it inside CRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous organised campaign for a cause, from the medieval holy wars.

clue.text: Dream trip?

parts.note: a dream is an imaginative fancy, and a trip is a flight, so the whole is a journey of the imagination

explanation.surface: A holiday one has always longed to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream trip' looks like an ideal holiday, but a flight here is the soaring of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an unrealistic idea or fantasy, the mind's soaring departure from reality.

clue.text: Minced tart seems rich but it's traditionally festive

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so these letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mince pie that tastes rich, a festive seasonal treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minced' rearranges TARTSEEMSRICH; the mince tart hints at the season too; 'but' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorated fir is a traditional centrepiece of December celebrations.

clue.text: Hint at rent reduction

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a fall is a reduction, as in a fall in prices

explanation.surface: A landlord suggesting that the rent might come down.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fall a remark is to mention it casually, dropping a hint.

clue.text: From end to end caused confusion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken and then entered under another spelling

parts.note: to throw someone is to confuse or disconcert them, so threw is the past tense

explanation.surface: A muddle stretching from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' changes the past tense of 'throw' into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Going right through something takes you along it completely from one side to the other.

clue.text: Last words of encouragement

explanation.surface: A coach's final pep talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to last or continue; and 'Go on!' is said to urge someone forward.

clue.text: American spy's backing military action, right

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ops is short for military operations
OK means all right or correct

explanation.surface: An American agent supports a military operation, all correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OPS into SPO; the 's is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spook is American slang for a secret agent.

clue.text: Full skirt?

parts.note: full here means full-length, a skirt reaching down to the ankles

explanation.surface: A wide flared skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full' suggests a wide, gathered skirt; it means one of full length.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a long skirt reaching the ankle, the opposite of a mini.

clue.text: Empty jug holding rum drink

indicators.note: holding says the shell keeps the word for strange inside it
Empty says the inner letters are removed, leaving the outer shell of the word

parts.note: a Toby jug is a pottery mug shaped like a seated man
rum is old slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An empty pitcher that once held a rum-based drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' cuts TOBY to TY; 'holding' puts ODD inside. 'rum' looks like the spirit but means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot alcoholic drink of spirits, sugar and water.

clue.text: Pen article before reaching Egyptian city

indicators.note: before puts the article in front of the bird

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A writer drafting an article before visiting Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is the female swan; 'reaching' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan is a city on the Nile in southern Egypt, known for its dam.

clue.text: Swimmer struggling in Po delta

indicators.note: struggling suggests something thrashing about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A swimmer in difficulties in the delta of Italy's River Po.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges PODELTA; 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A young frog or toad before metamorphosis lives in water and swims with its tail.

clue.text: Number accompanying old soldier not a problem

parts.note: an old sweat is slang for a veteran soldier

explanation.surface: Someone with an old soldier who is no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old sweat' is British slang for a veteran; 'accompanying' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means something is easy, with no effort or difficulty.

clue.text: Licence obtained without party member

parts.note: free of something is without it, as in free from care
a do is a party or celebration
M is a common abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A permit obtained without the help of a party politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained' is link; 'without' supplies the word meaning lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence and liberty are synonyms: the right to act as one wishes.

clue.text: International hot line?

parts.note: an imaginary line through many nations along the hottest part of the globe

explanation.surface: A telephone link set up between world leaders for emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotline is a direct phone link; here it is a hot line round the world crossing many countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle around Earth's middle passes through tropical countries on several continents.

clue.text: People going in came across old souvenir

indicators.note: going in says the people are put inside the word for encountered

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them
men are people

explanation.surface: Visitors entering a place came upon an antique keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' puts MEN inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept to remember a person or event, a keepsake.

clue.text: Second to complain, faced with one key singing role

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
I is the Roman numeral one
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A singer moaning briefly about one musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarpia is the villainous police chief in Puccini's opera Tosca; 'faced with' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Baron Scarpia is a baritone part in Tosca, a part sung on the opera stage.

clue.text: Tax period

explanation.definitionFit: To tax something is to strain it to its limit; and a stretch is a continuous spell of time.

clue.text: Plate is broken in exercises

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A plate smashed during a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PLATEIS; 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of controlled physical exercises for core strength.

clue.text: Accepted objection to border

parts.note: A is short for accepted, as on a list of replies
but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A complaint about a boundary dispute is accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut something is to touch or share a boundary with it.

clue.text: Turned out well when transport system's brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word is turned to run the other way

parts.note: trams run on rails as a city transport system

explanation.surface: A city transport scheme that was revived proved a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns TRAMS into the answer; 'when' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone turned out smart is neatly and fashionably dressed.

clue.text: Quick move in match, crossing line

indicators.note: crossing says the word for match spans the line, which sits inside it

parts.note: to fit is to match

explanation.surface: A rapid run in a football match, across the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside FIT; 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flit is a swift light movement, or a hasty departure.

clue.text: Some get husbands in this way

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some women find a spouse by this method.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is a formal adverb meaning so, or like this.

clue.text: Act to bring about revolution

explanation.surface: Taking action to start a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety act is a performer's spot on the bill; and to spin something round is to make it rotate.

clue.text: Get it and take off

explanation.surface: Grab the item and remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get it is to understand; and to take off is to become popular quickly.

clue.text: Charge has bearing on European administrator

parts.note: something held in trust is in one's charge
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: An accusation against a European official that bears on their conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee manages property or funds on behalf of others.

clue.text: Greek writer Persian has to put off

indicators.note: put off can mean disturbed or upset, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Greek author being postponed by a Persian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' rearranges PERSIANHASTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the comic playwright of ancient Athens who wrote The Frogs and The Birds.
